title: Fit a logistic regression two ways
brief: Build a stable sigmoid and log loss, their gradient and Hessian, then see Newton's method finish in a few steps where gradient descent needs hundreds.
hints: For softplus, use np.maximum(z, 0) + np.log1p(np.exp(-np.abs(z))). The value inside np.exp is never positive, so it can't overflow.
For sigmoid, build a mask pos = z >= 0. Use 1 / (1 + np.exp(-z)) on the positive part and np.exp(z) / (1 + np.exp(z)) on the rest.
The gradient is X.T @ (sigmoid(X @ w) - y) + ridge * w. No loop over examples is needed.
For the Hessian, let s = p * (1 - p). Then (X * s[:, None]).T @ X + ridge * np.eye(d) scales the rows of X without building a diagonal matrix.
A Newton step is delta = np.linalg.solve(hessian(...), gradient(...)), then w = w - delta. Keep the small ridge: it keeps the solve well posed on nearly separable data.
